reader.requirement: At --std 85, STRING must move characters one at a time into identifier-3 at the position the pointer designates, increase the pointer by one after each character actually moved (never when the pointer is already outside 1..size), and change identifier-4 by nothing else: after an overflow before any move it keeps its exact value, after a completed or truncated transfer it equals the start value plus the characters moved.

edition-consulted.switches: refuses a STRING whose last sending phrase omits DELIMITED (Constructs.StringDelimitedOmitted2002) at --std 85; a syntax arm, it does not touch the pointer or the transfer
nothing behavioural: BoundRejected.Report/BoundOperandError.Report(ctx.Edition, ...) only carry the edition context for SR diagnostics

reader.edition-search: grep of Edition|CobolVersion|Dialect|Construct in StringEmitter.cs and StringUnstringBinder.cs; grep of String|Unstring in Validation/VersionConformancePass.cs. EmitString and CobolStringOps.StringTransfer take no edition input: the implicit pointer of 1 and the per-character increment are one code path for every --std.

reader.notes: StringTransfer checks the pointer before each character, writes at pointer-1 and increments after; the emitter stores the POINTER item back only when it moved (ptr != ptr0), so an out-of-range start leaves it exact. The subscripts of sending items are frozen once (IdentifyOperands), so the pointer's own changes do not re-target a sender.

refuter.evidence: CobolStringOps.StringTransfer checks 1<=pointer<=size before each move and increments after it; EmitString stores the pointer back only when it moved, and does so BEFORE EmitOverflow. Probes (run_case.py, --std 85), t1-001: A: P=8 with '12345' prints 'A OVF P=11' from INSIDE ON OVERFLOW (the value is visible to imperative-statement-1), and [.......123]. B: a COMP S9(4) pointer goes 3 to +0006. C: a PIC 9 pointer, 8 characters into X(8), gives 9 with no overflow. D: receiver TE (I) with POINTER I, I=2: TBL [----QQ---------], I=4, so the receiver subscript stays frozen while the pointer changes. E: sender SRC (I:3) with POINTER I, I=2: [.BCD......], I=5 (the reference modifier is frozen).
